name: Prefab veneers (Snap-On Smile)

card.summary: Removable clip-on tooth covers sold as an instant smile; no research on them was found.
card.note: No clinical studies on removable veneers were found.

quick.overview:
Prefab veneers are removable shells meant to be worn over the teeth to alter how the smile looks. They are not bonded and can be taken out.

Unlike dentist-made veneers, they have little published evidence behind them.
quick.mechanism: A preformed cover fits over the existing teeth and is held in place by fit rather than by bonding.
quick.risks: No safety or effectiveness studies on removable veneers were found. Information on bonded veneers does not directly apply to them.

lead: Prefab or snap-on veneers are removable cosmetic covers that fit over the front teeth to change their apparent colour, shape and spacing without drilling or bonding. People use them as an immediate way to get a whiter, more even-looking smile, covering stains, chips, gaps or missing teeth, and can take them out again.[4]

They differ from bonded veneers, which are thin porcelain or composite coverings attached to the tooth, usually for discolouration, enamel defects, fractures and shape changes.[1] The best-documented branded version, Snap-On Smile, is a custom arch made by a dental laboratory in a thin resin from a dentist's impression, fitted over three visits, and described by its maker as removable and reversible.[4]

Published literature consists mainly of dentist-written clinical descriptions and case reports, including use in amelogenesis imperfecta, as an interim restoration before porcelain veneers, and as a non-invasive option for older patients; no controlled trials were found.[2][3][5]

angle.text: A removable cover changes how the teeth look the moment it is in place, so users get a brighter, more regular smile without altering their own teeth. The effect lasts only while it is worn.

paras: Dental veneers in the clinical sense are made mainly of composite or dental porcelain and bonded to the tooth; porcelain versions are made indirectly in a laboratory.[1] Removable snap-on products are a separate category held in place by fit rather than by bonding.[4]

The Snap-On Smile system is described by its maker as a custom removable arch that covers stains, chips, gaps and missing teeth. A dentist takes an impression, typically without injections, drilling or removal of tooth structure, a dental laboratory fabricates the arch and the dentist fits it at the final visit. It is marketed as an affordable, non-invasive alternative to veneers, implants or dentures, usable temporarily or long term, and the maker states that eating and drinking are possible while wearing it, with sticky foods avoided.[4]

A 2006 article in Dentistry Today describes clinical applications and two case studies of Snap-On Smile.[5][6] A 2015 case in the Journal of the Tennessee Dental Association used it for a preteen with amelogenesis imperfecta, a hereditary enamel disorder with discoloured, sensitive teeth, to improve appearance without altering the developing dentition.[3]

A 2020 article in the Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry describes snap-on provisional restorations for veneer cases, which patients can clean easily so soft tissues are healthier before final cementation; the authors describe it as an effective provisionalization option accepted by patients.[2] A 2016 case report describes a Snap-On-Smile overdenture for a 78-year-old with osteonecrosis of the jaw, restoring speech, function and esthetics.[7] A 2013 trade article presents it as a convenient option for older patients.[8]
No controlled studies found. Published work consists of clinical technique descriptions and case reports, mainly from dentists.[2][3][5][7]
